q: Developers working from home must reach an entire Azure virtual network from their personal laptops, including virtual machines, service endpoints, and a private file share.  They must use Azure private IP addresses for the connection.  What should you configure?

A subnet is associated with a Network Security Group (NSG) that contains two rules.  Rule1 has priority 100 and allows inbound traffic on port 80. Rule2 has priority 200 and denies inbound traffic on port 80.  How will inbound traffic on port 80 be handled?
options: Denied, because Deny rules always override Allow rules regardless of priority
Allowed, because Rule1 has the lower priority number
Denied, because Rule2 has the higher priority number
Blocked by the default inbound security rules
exp: Allowed, because Rule1 has the lower priority number

q: VNet-A contains Subnet-1 with VM-1. VNet-B contains Subnet-2 with VM-2, and Subnet-3 with VM-3. VNet-A and VNet-B are peered.  NSG-1 is associated with Subnet-1 and allows outbound RDP (TCP 3389) to Subnet-2 and to Subnet-3. NSG-2 is associated with Subnet-2 and allows inbound RDP (TCP 3389) from Subnet-1. NSG-3 is associated with Subnet-3 and allows inbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from Subnet-1. No other custom rules exist.  Which statement accurately describes RDP traffic originating from VM-1?
options: VM-1 to VM-2 is ALLOWED; VM-1 to VM-3 is BLOCKED
VM-1 to VM-2 is BLOCKED; VM-1 to VM-3 is ALLOWED
Both VM-1 to VM-2 and VM-1 to VM-3 are BLOCKED
Both VM-1 to VM-2 and VM-1 to VM-3 are ALLOWED
exp: VM-1 to VM-2 is ALLOWED; VM-1 to VM-3 is BLOCKED

q: VM1 is an Azure virtual machine that must be backed up every day.  Each recovery point must be kept for 30 days and then removed automatically.  The solution must minimize administrative effort.  What should you assign to the virtual machine?

VNet1 and VNet2 are deployed in the same Azure region and are peered.  Virtual machines in both virtual networks communicate over private IP addresses.  You deploy a third virtual network, VNet3, in the same region. Virtual machines in VNet3 must be able to reach virtual machines in VNet1 and in VNet2 using private IP addresses. The solution must require minimum administrative effort.  What should you configure?
options: A peering from VNet3 to VNet1 only, because peering is transitive
Azure Firewall in VNet1 to forward traffic to VNet2
A peering from VNet3 to VNet1 and a peering from VNet3 to VNet2
A Site-to-Site VPN Gateway between VNet3 and VNet1

q: You attempt to connect virtual machines between VNet1 and VNet2 over a virtual network peering connection.  Virtual machines in VNet1 can successfully communicate with virtual machines in VNet2, but virtual machines in VNet2 cannot initiate communication back to virtual machines in VNet1.  What is the most likely cause?
options: An inbound Network Security Group (NSG) rule on VNet1's subnet is blocking traffic
Virtual network peering cannot permit bi-directional traffic
The peering on VNet2 was created without 'Allow forwarded traffic'
A User-Defined Route on VNet2's subnet sends the traffic elsewhere
exp: An inbound Network Security Group (NSG) rule on VNet1's subnet is blocking traffic
